newsitem.title: JAPAN: TDK posts record profits as weak yen lifts sales.
newsitem.headline: TDK posts record profits as weak yen lifts sales.

text.p: Japanese electronic components manufacturer TDK Corp said on Friday that its profits surged to a record high last business year, as a weaker yen lifted sales in Asia and the Americas.
The firm said that its July 1996 sale of Silicon Systems Inc had generated a pretax gain of approximately 25 billion yen ($213 million).
"Even without this gain, however, operating profit, pretax and net earnings reached all-time highs," it said in a statement.

TDK, the world's largest manufacturer of magnetic tapes, said its group net profits totalled 60.30 billion yen ($515 million) in the year ended March 31, 1997, up 117.7 percent from 27.93 billion ($238 million) last year.
Operating profit rose 42.9 percent to 77.25 billion ($660 million) and pretax profit by 98.9 percent to 103.30 billion yen ($882 million).
A spokesman said that the firm's internal exchange rate for the past business year was set at 112 yen to the dollar.
TDK said its overseas sales jumped by 18.4 percent from the previous year, supported by large orders for electronic components and recording media.
Profits from overseas, where the firm has been investing aggressively in production facilities, accounted for 60.3 percent of consolidated net sales, up from 58.4 percent in the previous year.

Sales in the electronic materials and components sector and in recording media both rose by about 15 percent, while a substantial rise in sales of memory cards and other products more than offset a decrease in semiconductor sales, TDK said.
Semiconductor sales fell when Texas Instruments Inc acquired TDK's U.S. semiconductor subsidiary, Silicon Systems Inc, in July 1996, the company said.
Recording media sales were especially lifted by CD-ROM disk sales, which more than doubled in Japan and also rose in the United States and Europe, TDK said. ($1=117 yen)
